**Base rate (rough)**
- BTC's realized volatility is about 40–50% a year, or roughly 2.5–3% a day. Over about 10.5 days that works out to a one-standard-deviation move of about ±8–10%.
- A gain of about 4–4.5% is therefore roughly 0.5 standard deviations. With no drift, that implies very roughly a 30–35% chance of finishing above $85k.

- **Big tech earnings:** expected in late October.
- **FOMC meeting:** probably Oct 27–28, 2026. I haven't confirmed the dates.

criterios: This question resolves YES if the price of Bitcoin (BTC) in US dollars at the 00:00:00 UTC snapshot beginning October 31, 2026 is at or above $85,000. The resolver will use the CoinGecko Bitcoin historical data page (https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin/historical_data), where each dated row reports a 00:00:00 UTC price snapshot for that date: the row dated 2026-10-31 will be used. If the price value shown for the 2026-10-31 row is $85,000.00 or higher, the question resolves YES; otherwise NO. For example, a value of $85,250 resolves YES and a value of $84,900 resolves NO. If CoinGecko no longer publishes this data, the Bitcoin USD price at 00:00:00 UTC on October 31, 2026 from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used.
letra_pequena: Only Bitcoin (BTC) is relevant; no other cryptocurrency or wrapped/forked token counts. The relevant figure is the single 00:00:00 UTC snapshot value for the calendar date 2026-10-31 as reported by the source, not an intraday high/low or a volume-weighted average over the day.

(a) About 10.5 days. The outcome is fixed by CoinGecko's 00:00 UTC snapshot dated October 31, 2026.

(b) The status quo is NO. BTC is about $81,300–82,100, roughly 4.5% below $85,000. It has traded sideways at $80–84k for about a month and touched about $84k without reaching $85k.

(c) The reference class is BTC's roughly 10-day log returns. With daily volatility of about 2.1–2.5%, the 10.5-day standard deviation is about 7–8%. (e) YES scenario: Glassnode's possible local bottom near $80k holds. Strong big-tech earnings and a less hawkish FOMC than feared push BTC through resistance near $84.9k. Month-end and options-expiry flows then carry it to $85–88k by October 31.

(f) Only one value counts: the single 00:00 UTC snapshot in CoinGecko's row dated 2026-10-31. Intraday highs before then do not count. Reaching $85k mid-week and falling back would still resolve NO, so the bar is a little harder than "touches $85k". The FOMC on October 28 falls within the window and could add volatility either way.
